messages:
maria_r: Support just escalated a p95/p99 latency regression for AcmeCorp. Started ~10:45UTC after the v2.14 runtime rollout to canary. Customers seeing long tails on generate endpoints, p99 ~2.8s up from 420ms. They pasted traces and said it began immediately after traffic flip.

sam: assigned to eng-runtime. Can you drop the support payload and a couple of request_ids?

maria_r: pasted: request_id=acme-req-9923, acme-req-9930. Payload is standard chat generate, seq len ~256. They say it repros intermittently ~1/20.

alexg: looking at our canary dashboards — I see a spike in queue_time and service_time for the warm path. p95 increases line up with a bump in cold-kv-misses metric. Also see more kernel-selector fallbacks to slow path on a subset of hosts.

oncall-sre: ci-bot flagged a canary job at 10:40 that changed kernel selector heuristics (PR #3872). Rollout was gradual but 30% of canary got the new selector.

ci-bot: deploy bot: rollout v2.14-canary started 10:35UTC, kernel-selector:enable_fast_mmap=true rolled to 25% at 10:38, 60% at 10:42.

dave_k: hypothesis: selector change increases attempts to use a fast mmap kernel that requires KV cache prefetch; on misses we see synchronous cold fetch which blocks a token generator for long tail. Head-of-line blocking causes p99 spikes.

sam: good hypothesis. Can we reproduce in staging? Any config flag to flip back?

alexg: repro steps I ran on a 4-node staging canary:
```
# simulate warm/cold mix
ab -n 2000 -c 30 -p payload.json https://staging-api/redwood/generate
# payload has ~256 tokens, chat context ~700 tokens
```
Result: intermittent generator stalls ~1-2s on ~5% of requests. Stack shows thread waiting on kv_prefetch futex.

dave_k: mitigation options: 1) flip enable_fast_mmap=false on canary hosts (config rollback) 2) increase async prefetch concurrency to avoid sync waits 3) temporary traffic-split rollback to previous runtime. Which do we want?

maria_r: customers are complaining. Support requests immediate rollback to previously healthy runtime if safe.

oncall-sre: if we can flip the flag without full rollback that's faster. I can push config change to canary pool and monitor.

alexg: I'll prepare the config toggle. It's a runtime feature flag in /deploy/configs/runtime/kernel-selector.json. Change: "enable_fast_mmap": false.

sam: notify product and legal for any customer-impacting change? We should post an incident if >5% of production requests affected.

maria_r: AcmeCorp reporting 8% p99 failures (user visible). I'd call that outage. I'll start an incident channel after we confirm mitigation.

ci-bot: config job queued: toggle kernel-selector.enable_fast_mmap -> false on canary cluster. Job id cfg-9981.

oncall-sre: pushed cfg-9981 at 10:52. Monitoring: within 2 mins p95 dropped back near baseline, p99 improved but still slightly above normal. Queue_time graphs show the cold-kv-miss latency back down.

alexg: follow-up: still seeing a tail on some older GPU hosts — those hosts didn't pick up the new prefetch settings because they run older sidecar. I'll open a canary host audit.

dave_k: next steps checklist: 
- [ ] fully rollback kernel-selector in canary and stop v2.14 rollout
- [ ] add async-prefetch fallback so fast_mmap doesn't block on miss
- [ ] schedule postmortem to review selector heuristics and rollout gating tests
- [ ] notify affected customers and offer credits if SLA breached

sam: I'm going to pause the v2.14 rollout until we confirm fixes. Maria, please coordinate customer comms and incident channel.

maria_r: will do. Opening incident now: #inc-406789. Adding affected customer notes and support thread links.

alexg: quick note for postmortem: include simple perf tests simulating KV cache churn and cold-prefetch to catch this in future canaries. Also instrument selector to emit downgrade reasons to tracing.

maria_r: thanks all — keeping AcmeCorp updated. Will post incident summary once stable. :white_check_mark:
